subsubtopic: FINANCIAL STATEMENT OF THE MIN ISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext:
Mr. Speaker, I must say, quite frankly, that ever since 5 p.m. on Thursday May 23,
I have been absolutely bursting with enthusiasm. That day, at 4.30 p.m., the Minister of Finance (Mr. Wilson) finally decided to do what no politician had done before, which is to act. Before that day, the word deficit sent shivers up and down my spine, as it does even now, but I can say now: We have a handle on it, things are going to start moving. After all, it is the Progressive Conservatives, not the Liberals. Mr. Speaker, since May 23 I have been terribly excited. Whenever I meet people, in my riding or elsewhere, they are talking about the Budget. I have yet to meet a single person, except for the Opposition, of course, who is against the Budget. Everyone is saying it was high time we chopped Government spending, it was high time we stopped Government waste, and I for one am proud to be a Progressive Conservative.
Mr. Speaker, I am sure my dear Liberal friends are going to say: O.K., but what about jobs? Believe me, if we cannot get jobs by reducing the deficit, they certainly did not get any by increasing it, because at the rate their deficit was going, we would have had minus zero jobs and minus zero unemployment insurance. The unemployment rate was at 10, 11 or 12 per cent and varied from time to time because to get the rate to go down a mere fraction, they would send three people out to work and that would do the trick. That is exactly what they have been doing during the last 18 years.
Upon analyzing the Budget of the Minister of Finance, we see that for once, a Government has had the good sense to stop minding other people's business and let small business take over. I thought there were only half a million small companies, but during the debate on the Budget, I heard, and I did not

May 31, 1985
The Budget-Mr. Jourdenais
know this there are 700,000 small companies, 700,000 companies that could be helped, but not like the Liberals used to do. They would say: Here, take $200,000, shut up and work. You don't need ideas or enthusiasm. Spend the money, there is more where that came from. Now this Government is saying: We will help you but you will have to show what you can do. Which reminds me, I had a terrific argument last week with a Liberal, and I told him: When you went to school, they gave you a gold star if you got good marks on your test. But under the Liberals during the last 18 years, people were given gold stars before, not after. That does not make sense. They seem to be pretty intelligent people and they are supposed to be very able and some of them are economists, teachers, lawyers, in fact, people from every walk of life. They are supposed to be intelligent, but as soon as they get to Parliament, that's it!
I can tell you, quite honestly, I am a small businessman from a region that is as big as Saint-Henri and Point Saint Charles. I always hear the Hon. Member for Saint-Henri-Westmount (Mr. Johnston) saying: My people in Saint-Henri, but he is really only concerned about the people on the other side of the hill. They are going to be as pleased as Punch. And we did not do what he said, which was we ought to tax businessmen. I think he would have to shell out his whole Member's salary if we decided to tax him, because he comes from the top of the hill!
1 have been a Conservative since 1 was 18, which means that I was fighting against arrogance all that time. I have heard people indulging in petty politics since the age of 18. I see some Members rising now, and in fact, one Member rose earlier and said: Enough petty politics! It is not true, I did not speak four times. I have risen in the House three times in four years. That is what is happening to him. I have been waiting for this opportunity for a long time, for weeks and months. And finally the Budget came and now i am going to say what I think of the previous Government. There was one of them, I think his name was Trudeau. Trudeau was the leader. Today people tell me that I am lucky because I can talk to Brian. We do not say Mr. Mulroney, we do not say Mr. Prime Minister, we say Brian. That is what the Progressive Conservative Party is all about, that is why we have a Budget which will help the people in my riding, as it will those in Saint-Henri and Westmount, believe me.
When I came here I decided I would sit on several committees because 1 really wanted to work, 24 hours a day, seven days a week, and 30 or 31 days a month. I recall a minor incident that hurt and upset me. One evening I attended a sitting of the Committee on Regional Economic Expansion where we were discussing those programs and how the famous Liberal system of patronage hand-outs worked. We were listening ot the explanations, then all of a sudden we were interrupted by a man who came in, a Quebec Minister of Expansion who looked at us and said: I must tell you, I have just managed to obtain more, and I was able to make myself
better understood in two hours than I ever could in six years with the Liberal Party. That is harmony, that is understanding, that is the Progressive Conservative Party.
Since September, or in fact since November we have begun to show how Government should be run. There have been many changes in immigration, new employment and training programs, and there are more to come. Believe me, I will make sure that unwarranted hand-outs are a thing of the past. We have launched quite a few regional economic expansion projects and awarded contracts in energy and resources from one end of the country to the other, and we did not even have a Budget. It is fantastic! Well, we have a Budget now, so just watch out, there will be lots of jobs because we have just told businessmen: Go ahead, we will not lead you by the hand, we will stay out of your business, we will give you tax credits. People will get down to work and invest their extra earnings in Pointe-Saint-Charles, Saint-Henri and La Prairie instead of buying boats, going down to Florida or travelling through foreign countries.
The Minister of State for Science and Technology (Mr. Siddon) said earlier that he was going to sell a property he has in the United States. Let me tell you that the Progressive Conservative Government is honest and open, and it will stand as an example for other people. Lots of people own a business or a building, or have something they could sell to make a capital gain. I am sure my colleague from Saint-Henri-West-mount has had 15 or 20 offers to sell his business under the table so he would not have to pay the capital gains tax-better to keep the money for himself. I am sure this sort of thing has happened. I have businesses, I have industries. Well, a business rather than an industry. I own commercial buildings and I have had offers not so long ago, but I said to myself: Just a minute, things are going to change. Everything will be in the open, you will be able to act honestly, and then you can invest your money and create jobs. That is what I have decided to do.
What I like about this Budget is that it will help small businesses, the corner stone of our economy. We are going to tell the businessman: Help yourself, then we will help you. The Liberals did as they would have done with a six-month old child. You hold his hand when he starts to walk. When the child is 10 years old, he is still being held by the hand. At 15, he is still being held by the hand, but he has become an invalid and he no longer wants to help himself. That is when businesses go bankrupt, like Maislin did. It is exactly the same situation. Maislin Transport on Newman Boulevard got $5 million, my friend, so that they could spend it.
When I look at the deficit, being a businessman, I ask myself how intelligent people in Parliament could have decided to stay in the red, as we, business people, would say. To show a deficit is to be in the red. They would have gone on being in the red. If we had a company as large as the Government, I
May 31, 1985

can assure you that not one businessman, not one financier, not one bank, and certainly not the Hon. Member for Saint-Henri-Westmount (Mr. Johnston), would be willing to lend it any money. You can bet on it no one would want to.
You know, some will say, and it is unfortunate that he is no longer here, the Hon. Member for ... I am sorry, but I cannot say that. 1 no longer call him "the Hon. Member for Mont-real-Sainte-Marie" but the champion of old age pensions that he failed to defend when his Party was in power. It is unfortunate that he is not in the House because I would have liked to tell him something. I am sorry, Mr. Speaker, but we are not supposed to say that someone is not in the House. He was here earlier. He had promised that he would listen to me. I hope that he is watching on television. Some have said that, by deindexing the old age security pensions, we would take $50 or $100 away from senior citizens. Astronomical figures have been mentioned. People are being scared, and it is exactly what happened in Quebec in 1976 with Brinks, for those who remember, and there also had been an election at the time. I must say that I really like senior citizens. In my constituency, there are 31 or 32 senior citizens' organizations. I take care of them, but there are about 12,000, 15,000, 18,000 or 20,000 young people whom I do not want to put into debt, children who have not even started to walk yet. My grandson, who is 2 years old, already has a $24,000 debt, and because of whom? Because of the former Liberal Government. Believe me, I have nothing against the elderly, because they have built Canada and they have helped us. If they worked hard during their lifetime, they will understand. They will not let themselves be deceived by the free spenders in the New Democratic Party, those charitable people who play Santa Claus. They do not even have any money and they want to give it away. For their part, the Liberals say: "It is dangerous, you will not get it. You will not be able to buy a pound of butter. You will not be able to buy such and such a thing." As recently as yesterday, I saw a Liberal Member eating chocolate even though it is now taxable. She did not care about her grandfather and grandmother. She did the same thing.
I could go on the whole afternoon. Believe me, I like it, because all this has to come out. I have been waiting for a long time to say these things. I could speak about the famous grants. Apparently, that is not what caused the deficit to increase. Apparently, they created one-, two- or three-week jobs. That is what those grants did. I would like to tell you a story about my constituency. However, I would like to tell you first about a whopper. During my campaign, when I said that I would abolish tolls on Champlain Bridge, I was asked: Where will you get the money? With the sports car that belonged to Minister Olivier from Longueuil. That was $1.5 million a week and I needed $3 million in one year. It was a cinch. However, when the Conservatives were elected, we said: This has to be cut. We already had saved of $1.5 billion even before the Budget. It is great.
The Budget-Mr. Jourdenais
I have another one I could tell you about the constituency of Longueuil. If someonw wants to buy a museum . . . there is one for cheap sale. I do not know how the Liberal grant was called at the time, but in my eyes it was a slush fund, a money bucket, a money spender. They built a museum worth $ 1,400,000 that is now on sale for $40,000 because the organization that was to operate it does not have the money to do so. It is going for $40,000. That is business management for you! With that, you will have a job and you will be somebody! They cal! that helping small businesses! True! And then they cry and lament, they scare people and they say: Watch out, you will you no longer be able to afford chocolate, toothpaste, or whatever. This is just too bad, my dear friends, but it is not the mere $50 tax difference or $1 if you want per day, as the Liberals have been clamouring about for I do not know how long. If it is not worth $1 to be a Canadian, my friend, it is not worth a peanut, and that is just too bad.
I am a Member of the Standing Committee on Labour, Employment and Immigration ... Concerning the Liberals again, I have a file that thick, believe me, that thick, of people ready to put $100,000 and $200,000 to come to Canada. Surely it is not that bad here. Those are not refugees, people in dire straits, hungry people. They are people with money, and if we do not have money, we will not go through.
The Hon. Member for Saint-Henri-Westmount (Mr. Johnston) must be aware of it. My examples relate to the richest people. This is the way things go. He does not remember me. The first year he was elected, he came to one of my shops. I remember. I did not vote for him. Do not fret about it. I did not vote for him because I was not in his constituency.
I could mention a grant in my constituency. This is what 1 am against, the wasting of money. You are going to say: The Budget, he only talks about that. Yes, because it is important to stop throwing money around. I have nothing against charitable institution. I have nothing against non-profit organizations, but I cannot stand people picking my pockets, especially against my will, to give it away as Government grants. He told two or three people: Shut up and go to work, this will do. We create jobs. Sometimes we were lucky, they lasted 48 hours.
In my constituency, I was lucky enough to open, believe it or not, a youth center, and this made headlines, believe me! 1 am allowed to quote the name of the guy I defeated, Pierre Deniger. He gave a $700,000 gift to a youth organization called "Intersection Jeunesse", a very five organization, very laudable goal, very good idea, but alas, they had forgotten about the revenues needed to operate the building from then on. Since I have been elected here, I have been fighting, trying to help them, not by getting funds here, but by helping 10, 12 organizations to make sure that this organization will keep afloat. I did not do it with money takes from the Hon. Member for Saint-Henri-Westmount (Mr. Johnston) or the Hon. Member for St. Maurice (Mr. Chretien) or any other Member. I think the Hon. Member for Ahuntsic, in Montreal,

May 31, 1985
The Budget-Mr. Jourdenais
would be willing to help with her money, not with Government money. Well, that organization just sold the building, believe it or not, for $1. This is what they call doing business, $700,000 for $1. You do not go bankrupt by charging 25 cents for a package of cigarettes, but by selling something worth $700,000 for $1, a museum for $90,000, $700,000 worth for $1.00. Surely, they know nothing about business.
I have so many things to say, Mr. Speaker, that 1 do not know where to start. Yes, indexation. The famous 3 per cent was discussed. 1 think the cost of living index is at 4.5 per cent right now, so an indexation of 1.5 per cent will be allowed.

3.9 per cent, this is even better, thank you. That means pensioners will get an indexation of 1 per cent and will lose 3 per cent. Have you ever thought that the Liberals were to blame for this regrettable 3 per cent contribution? They should not have made my father and my grandmother pay. It is awful to make them pay. But the cost of living will not get higher. For instance, products will not cost more because we will see to it and we will put small industries to work; we will help small business operators, not only one, two or three, but 700,000 small businessmen. Have you thought about it? There will be no more unemployment. I own a small business and I know it will be the easiest thing to do. I remember something now that I forgot to tell the Opposition. If I were given $700,000, I would create fifty jobs that would last twenty years. That is the amount that was given in my riding to create about fifty jobs for a month and a half. That is interesting.
I repeat that I have been a member of this party since I was 18. I heard someone say in 1974 that the 5 to 6 per cent controls Mr. Stanfield was proposing to increase profits was not a good proposal. Then the man who came into office, what was his name, I forget? Trudeau! He said: Now that we are the Government, the proposal makes send. Do you not see that the Liberals change their minds when they change sides in the House? Once in office they implemented policies taken from the Conservative Government they said they did not like. The same thing happened in 1979. The Clark Government was defeated. Why? For 30 cents worth of gas. That was increased to $1.18 once the Liberals were back into office. They had plenty of money that did not come from their pockets but from those of all the taxpayers. It is about time this should be stopped.
Mr. Speaker, I still have five minutes, right?

speechtext:
My goodness, I must hurry!
I sit on the House Standing Committee on Employment and Immigration. There are 20,000 outstanding cases. I do not know how much that costs because the system developed by
the previous Government is too fouled-up. I cannot say. There is nothing one can do but leave one's name and wait until Mr. So-and-So of one of the departments get hold of the file. It may take as many as four years. What is the cost? Who cares? The people of Canada, the people of Laprairie, Saint-Henri and Westmount also, my friend, are the ones who will pay. 1 should like to reply to the Hon. Member for Montreal-Sainte-Marie (Mr. Malepart) who complained about the new uniforms for the Armed Forces. We cannot let them walk around naked, damn it! Do not try to con me into believing that red, blue, yellow or green uniforms-I should have left red out- will cost more than bottle-green ones. Do not bother me, for we must clothe our soldiers so they will look like something to be proud of, instead of a gang of nincompoops who could not be found in the fields because their uniforms were the same colour as the trees.
We are going to help people, starting for instance with widows and widowers 60 to 64 years of age. When they were the government, they used to limit the pensions to senior citizens over 65. Those who were only 64 would have to kick the bucket before getting a pension. We want to give it to them when they reach age 60. They insist on our paying the pension to people who are separated, divorced or what have you. One day, have no fear, they will get it. We will lower the age limit and we will have the money to do that, thanks to the small businesses which are supporting us.
Because I am running out of time, Mr. Speaker, 1 will take a sip of water and explain something that will knock over all those who are still here. Believe it or not, I have just learned, and I would appreciate the members of the opposition- [English]
-so that you would listen, especially to those who were in power before, who thought they were in power.
I have just heard that in my constituency there are $3 million worth of goods for Bolivia, I repeat, $3 million, packed in containers since January 1982. What about that? speechtext:
He has brought several things to our attention.
I think it behooves us all to read his speech when we receive Hansard on Monday because there is a lot of thought and merit in it.
The Hon. Member has raised the issue of waste. The Budget does deal with the reality that 80 per cent of the deficit cuts are coming through reduced expenditures. We on this side of the House are looking for as much waste and as much duplication as we can find. I wonder if the Hon. Member might tell us how he became aware of these examples? I suspect that people in his riding brought them to his attention. If that was the case, perhaps he could inform us. I think we are all looking for those examples of waste wherever we can find them, and we need as much help as we can get. Would the Hon. Member share with us his thoughts as to how he found out about these examples?

subsubtopic: FINANCIAL STATEMENT OF THE MIN ISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext:
Mr. Speaker, 1 thank the Hon. Member for his question. I got the documents and I know what is happening in my riding because I returned to my riding last week-end and gave a speech to people who have decided to bring their organization under control. They need $600,000 and already have $100,000. They told me: "We will not have to go very far

May 31, 1985
The Budget-Mr. Waddell
to find the money, because there is some lying around in the yard over there." This is exactly what I was told. Because I am a government Member who wants to help people and not waste money, I decided to have a look. So I went there and discovered $3 million worth of goods which have been in containers since 1982, two trucks which have never been moved, which have never been used. They were supposed to- [English]
-for Bolivia. 1 don't know why it is there. I am sure there must be some other examples of waste because this was done by the previous administration, which worked in this way. I am positive that there must be some millions, probably in Liberal ridings, perhaps not now in Conservative ridings but probably in Liberal ridings. So this is the way I found out. If you want to know more-

-come and see me and I will tell everything because right after I think I will have a press conference.

speechtext:
Since there are no further questions for the Hon. Member, we shall resume debate.
